submission.justification: Selection-S2 has the highest documented expected significance (4.1 sigma at 50% signal efficiency), but the validation-region study shows a 35% data/MC yield disagreement driven by poorly modelled jet-substructure inputs. That is well outside the 10% tolerance agreed with the physics conveners, so its background estimate is not robust and it is excluded by the robustness constraint. Among the remaining options, Selection-S3 (neural network on kinematic variables) gives 3.4 sigma expected significance at 50% signal efficiency, versus 2.6 sigma for the cut-based Selection-S1. S3's 6% yield disagreement is within the 10% tolerance, while S1 is better modelled (3%) but has lower sensitivity. S3 is therefore the recommended strategy with the 50% working point, which is inside the 20-80% range. Caveats: I did not have access to a Monte Carlo sensitivity tool in this session, so the significances are taken from the 2025 summary (statistical uncertainty only, not re-optimised for the working point). The 6% S3 disagreement should be folded into the systematic uncertainty before the result is quoted, and a scan of the working point under the full systematic model is recommended before unblinding.
